answer: At the ridge station the keeper reads the wind and temperature every hour, and the readings fill a log that runs without a gap for years. A timber reading written in one sitting fails the log: at the velvet of the entry the ink and handwriting must vary hour by hour, and a fresh forgery shows one sitting. Faking three years of readings means hiring a keeper to live at the station and paying 31,000 in wages, and the nebula book is countersigned monthly by the observatory, so a gap in the signatures gives the fraud away.
